info.bio: Don van Vliet nacido como Don Glenn Vliet y conocido como Captain Beefheart (15 de enero de 1941 – 17 de diciembre de 2010) fue un músico de rock y pintor estadounidense originario de Glendale, California, Estados Unidos. Su trabajo musical lo realizó acompañado por una banda llamada The Magic Band, que estuvo activa desde mediados de los 60 hasta principios de los 80. Van Vliet principalmente dirigía la banda y tocaba la armónica y, ocasionalmente, el saxofón y el teclado, de manera amateur e influenciado por el free-jazz.

scenes.name: Excéntricos y art rock de los setenta
scenes.book: Postpunk. Romper todo y empezar de nuevo
scenes.author: Simon Reynolds
scenes.desc: El mito punk del «páramo» prepunk escondía uno de los periodos más ricos del rock. Con cautela, para no parecer hippies encubiertos, los grupos postpunk recuperan a excéntricos como Captain Beefheart y las aristas más agudas del progresivo: Soft Machine, King Crimson, incluso Frank Zappa. «En cierto sentido, el postpunk era rock progresivo» racionalizado, sin virtuosismo.
scenes.family: Antecedentes: punk, art rock, kraut y glam

scenes.name: Los freaks de Los Ángeles: Zappa y Beefheart
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El genio supremo de la contracultura, Frank Zappa, no conoce barreras de estilo ni reglas de armonía: coinventa el álbum conceptual, la ópera rock y el rock progresivo, usa el estudio como instrumento y compone con fragmentos de músicas preexistentes, todo al servicio de la sátira. Captain Beefheart, quizá el mayor músico de rock de todos los tiempos (el único con 214), mezcla blues del Delta, free jazz y vanguardia con estructuras oblicuas y dementes; Trout Mask Replica es «la principal contribución del rock a la historia de la música».

scenes.name: Rock sureño
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Los estados del sur desarrollan sus propias vibraciones «duras», enraizadas en el boogie y el honky-tonk de los saloons. Los Allman Brothers, primera gran banda desde los Grateful Dead para la que el directo improvisado importa más que el disco (Live At Fillmore East); ZZ Top, enciclopedia de estilos sureños (Tres Hombres); la oscura Hampton Grease Band; Lynyrd Skynyrd y el estilo de vida del macho sureño reaccionario; Outlaws.

scenes.name: Cruces del punk: de Fugazi al punk-pop
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: A finales de los ochenta el punk es el más vivo de los subgéneros del rock: miles de bandas ensayando en garajes, un lenguaje universal como no se veía desde los sesenta. Nueva York: Adrenalin O.D., el straight-edge de Youth Of Today y Gorilla Biscuits, el crossover punk-metal (Cro-Mags, Prong, Danzig). Washington lanza a Pussy Galore (la irrelevancia hecha relevante), Unrest y Fugazi de Ian MacKaye, que abstrae el hardcore en una forma teatral de compromiso ético y estético (Repeater, Steady Diet Of Nothing, Red Medicine), y Royal Trux (Twin Infinitives, «un Trout Mask Replica para la generación grunge»). El punk-pop de Mr T Experience, Dwarves, Henry Rollins, L7 (pioneras del «foxcore»), Lemonheads, Screeching Weasel, Goo Goo Dolls, Fastbacks, Shonen Knife; el «rogue folk» de los Pogues, Membranes y Chumbawamba.
scenes.family: Punk, new wave, hardcore y noise

podcast.title: A&M Records Signing and Antics
podcast.body: Captain Beefheart and His Magic Band signed with A&M Records in 1966, an indie label co-founded by Herb Alpert. The label was notably indulgent of Beefheart over the years, despite his unpredictable behavior. One anecdote describes him showing up at the label's offices with a loaded crossbow, angered by criticism of his work. "Beefheart and his magic band were eventually signed to An M in 1966 and over the years the label indulged him a lot, even though he would do things like show up with a loaded crossbow at the offices because he was angry that somebody dared critique his work."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: A&M Signing and Eccentric Behavior
podcast.body: Captain Beefheart and his Magic Band signed with A&M Records in 1966, where the label largely indulged his eccentricities. This included an incident where he reportedly showed up at the A&M offices with a loaded crossbow, angered by criticism of his work. "Beefheart and his magic band were eventually signed to An M in 1966, and over the years the label indulged him a lot, even though he would do things like show up with a loaded crossbow at the offices just because he was angry that somebody dared critique his work."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Artistic Background and Dyslexia
podcast.body: Born Don Van Vliet, Captain Beefheart was primarily a sculptor and painter before his music career, showing enthusiasm for various forms of artistic expression. He was a close friend of Frank Zappa. He was also very dyslexic and claimed to have never attended public school, a statement later proven untrue but contributing to his enigmatic persona. "Beefheart was mainly a sculptor and a painter, but he was enthusiastic for all sorts of artistic expression which inevitably led to music."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Disputed Public School Claim
podcast.body: Van Vliet falsely claimed to have never attended public school, a fabrication that nonetheless "makes for a great story." "He claimed to have never gone to public school, which is not true, but it makes for a great story."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Life and Artistic Pursuits
podcast.body: Born Don Van Vliet, he was a close friend of Frank Zappa and primarily engaged in sculpting and painting, demonstrating an enthusiasm for all forms of artistic expression, which eventually led him to music. He was very dyslexic and deeply admired rhythm and blues. "Beefheart was mainly a sculptor and a painter, but he was enthusiastic for all sorts of artistic expression, which inevitably led to music."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Influence on Experimentation
podcast.body: Captain Beefheart's ability to create and release such an experimental and unconventional record as *Trout Mask Replica* served as a significant inspiration for other artists, encouraging them to embrace experimentation and difference in their own music. "If he could make a record, others thought, well then so could I."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Influence on Future Artists
podcast.body: Captain Beefheart's 1969 album "Trout Mask Replica," despite its un-listenable quality to many, was bought and absorbed by a lot of people who would later go on to do "cool things," signifying its lasting impact and influence. "And again it's important because a lot of people who would later go on to do cool things, bought that album and absorbed it."

podcast.title: Sculptor Turned Musician
podcast.body: Before his musical career, Captain Beefheart (Don Van Vliet) was a sculptor based in California. He transitioned into music, releasing his profoundly strange album "Trout Mask Replica" in the fall of 1969. "That October, a California sculptor turned musician named Captain Befart released an album that was so strange that it immediately became an underground classic."

xref.title: Robert Smith's Early Influences
xref.body: Robert Smith's older siblings introduced him to a diverse range of artists, including The Beatles, The Rolling Stones, Captain Beefheart, David Bowie, Jimi Hendrix, and Nick Drake. The subsequent arrival of punk rock, with bands like Sex Pistols, Ramones, and Elvis Costello, further shaped his musical direction and helped him find his artistic niche. "His older brother and sister had filled his head with beetles and stone songs, but they also subjected him to a lot of Captain B-Fart, and David Bowie, and Jimmy Hendrix and Nick Drake. And then when punk came along, it was Sex Pistols Ramones Elvis Costello. Young Robert found his niche."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Robert Smith's Influences
xref.body: Robert Smith's musical upbringing was shaped by his older brother and sister, who introduced him to The Beatles and The Rolling Stones. They also exposed him to more unconventional artists like Captain Beefheart, David Bowie, Jimi Hendrix, and Nick Drake. The arrival of punk further influenced Smith, with bands like the Sex Pistols, Ramones, and Elvis Costello helping him discover his artistic niche. "His older brother and sister had filled his head with beetles and stone songs, but they also subjected him to a lot of Captain B. Fart, and David Bowie, and Jimmy Hendrix and Nick Drake."

xref.title: Struggling for Image and Sound (Late 1960s)
xref.body: Around the time The Velvet Underground, The Stooges, MC5, and Captain Beefheart were making records, David Bowie was struggling to define his own image, style, and sound, without much success. "Well, he was trying to find himself. He was trying to come up with an image and a style and a sound that would work for him and he wasn't doing very well."
